mainTopic: Whether executions override שבת (the ברייתא of "לא תבערו"), and why the word עליה is needed, using the rules of דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא
overview: The גמרא is explaining a ברייתא that uses the פסוק "לא תבערו" to teach that בית דין does not carry out executions on שבת. רב שמי בר אשי says the ברייתא's first idea, that executions might override שבת, came from a קל וחומר: execution overrides עבודה, and עבודה overrides שבת. The puzzling words "או אינו" are read as an attempt to break that קל וחומר from קבורת מת מצוה. The attempt fails, so the פסוק is needed. The גמרא then explains "או אינו" according to its earlier reading, in which the תנא went back and forth over whether an עשה can override a לאו that carries כרת. Next the גמרא gives a new reason why the word עליה is needed in the יבום פרשה. One might apply the rule of דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא מן הכלל ללמד and permit all עריות, the way the example of שלמים teaches about all קדשי מזבח. The גמרא rejects this comparison, because אשת אח is permitted while her group is forbidden. It says her case fits a different rule instead: something that left its group for a new law, יצא לידון בדבר החדש. A ברייתא illustrates that rule with the אשם of a מצורע, and its explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The קל וחומר: execution should override שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב שמי בר אשי's explanation continues. Since executing a murderer overrides עבודה, and עבודה overrides שבת, execution should surely override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Temple service is so serious that it overrides שבת, and yet executing a murderer overrides the Temple service (as the פסוק says, "From My altar you shall take him to die"), then שבת, which gives way to the Temple service, should surely give way to executing a murderer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב שמי בר אשי's explanation. He says the ברייתא's first idea, that executions might happen on שבת, came from a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument has three links. First, עבודה is stronger than שבת. Second, execution is stronger than עבודה, because a murderer is taken even from the מזבח. So execution should also be stronger than שבת. This idea comes from logic and does not depend on the rule of עשה דוחה לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple service, such as bringing קרבנות
Murder; here it means executing a convicted murderer
"From My altar you shall take him to die": a murderer is taken even from the Temple service
"Is it not logical?": the standard closing line of a קל וחומר
Is pushed aside / overridden

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the ברייתא's first idea may have come from a logical argument and not from עשה דוחה לא תעשה. The rest of the passage is built on that point.

phrases.english: If the Temple service, which is severe,
and overrides Shabbat,
murder overrides it,
phrases.notes: "Murder" here is short for executing a murderer. That execution beats the Temple service.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "From My altar you shall take him to die,"
then Shabbat, which is pushed aside by the Temple service,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁתְּהֵא רְצִיחָה דּוֹחָה אוֹתָהּ?
phrases.english: is it not logical that murder should override it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה עֲבוֹדָה, שֶׁהִיא חֲמוּרָה וְדוֹחָה שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב שמי בר אשי's explanation of the ברייתא, which began before this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By קל וחומר, execution would override שבת, because it overrides עבודה, which itself overrides שבת.

steps.title: What does "or perhaps not" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by its confusing phrase "או אינו".
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the "or perhaps it is not" that the תנא said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a confusing phrase in the ברייתא. This sets up the next step, which explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes back and forth, saying "או אינו", as if it has a reason to doubt the קל וחומר. The גמרא wants to know what that doubt is according to רב שמי בר אשי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: "Or perhaps it is not": a phrase that brings up the other possibility
"And what?": asking for an explanation
"That he said"

phrases.english: And what is the "or perhaps it is not" that he said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the ברייתא's wording fits the קל וחומר just presented.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the "או אינו" in the ברייתא refers to, given that the reasoning was a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Burial of a מת מצוה seems to break the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: "או אינו" means the תנא tried to knock down the קל וחומר using קבורת מת מצוה. It overrides עבודה, yet it does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: burying a מת מצוה proves otherwise. It overrides the Temple service, yet it does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that "או אינו" is the תנא's attempt to break the קל וחומר. He uses an example where something overrides עבודה but still does not override שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that anything stronger than עבודה must also be stronger than שבת. קבורת מת מצוה seems to show that this is not true. If so, execution might also beat עבודה without beating שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Burying a dead person who has no one else to bury him
"Will prove": a counterexample that breaks a קל וחומר
"This is what he is saying": the גמרא explains the real meaning

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
the burial of a met מצוה will prove otherwise,
for it overrides the Temple service,
and yet it does not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: קְבוּרַת מֵת מִצְוָה תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "או אינו" is an attempt to refute the קל וחומר using קבורת מת מצוה, which overrides עבודה but not שבת.

steps.title: The תנא pushes back: burial should also override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The תנא takes back the refutation. By the same קל וחומר, קבורת מת מצוה itself should override שבת, so it cannot serve as a counterexample.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he said: burying a מת מצוה should itself override שבת by a קל וחומר. If the Temple service overrides שבת, and burying a מת מצוה overrides the Temple service (we learn this from "or for his sister"), then שבת, which gives way to the Temple service, should surely give way to burying a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא changes his mind about the counterexample. He argues that the same logic would make קבורת מת מצוה override שבת as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A counterexample only works if its own law is fixed. But the very same קל וחומר could be applied to קבורת מת מצוה, so on logic alone it is not proven that burial does not override שבת. That leaves the קל וחומר for execution standing. In the middle, the גמרא stops to give the source showing that burial overrides עבודה: "ולאחותו".

keyTerms.meaning: "He then said": the speaker takes back or changes his earlier point
"Should override"
Reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter one
"Or for his sister": an extra word in the פסוק about a נזיר

steps.confusionAlert: The words "מ׳ולאחותו׳" are not part of the קל וחומר itself. They are a short side remark giving the source for why burial overrides עבודה. After them, the קל וחומר picks up again.

phrases.english: He then said:
the burial of a met מצוה should override Shabbat
by a kal vachomer:
If the Temple service, which overrides Shabbat,
is overridden by the burial of a met מצוה,
as we learn from "or for his sister,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:7. The extra word teaches that even a נזיר on his way to bring the קרבן פסח becomes טמא to bury a מת מצוה.

phrases.english: then Shabbat, which is pushed aside by the Temple service,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁתְּהֵא קְבוּרַת מֵת מִצְוָה דּוֹחָה אוֹתָהּ?
phrases.english: is it not logical that the burial of a met מצוה should override it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר: קְבוּרַת מֵת מִצְוָה תִּדְחֶה שַׁבָּת מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counterexample of step 3 by applying the same קל וחומר to it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the refutation from קבורת מת מצוה, which brings the original קל וחומר back.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The counterexample's own law (that burial does not override שבת) could itself be overturned by the same קל וחומר.

steps.title: The פסוק "לא תבערו" settles it
steps.stepSummary: Since logic would let both execution and burial override שבת, the פסוק "לא תבערו" is needed to teach that they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the פסוק teaches: "You shall not kindle fire in all your dwellings on the day of שבת."
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא brings the פסוק "לא תבערו" to stop the קל וחומר. This finishes רב שמי בר אשי's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic alone could not block the קל וחומר. So the תורה had to say outright that executions do not override שבת. This explains why the ברייתא needed a פסוק at all.

keyTerms.meaning: "The פסוק teaches": a פסוק that settles the question
"You shall not kindle": the פסוק that teaches executions are not done on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב שמי בר אשי, the ברייתא's hesitation came from a קל וחומר (execution beats עבודה, which beats שבת). קבורת מת מצוה could not break it, so the פסוק "לא תבערו" was needed to teach that executions do not override שבת.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "You shall not kindle."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the קל וחומר survived the refutation, the פסוק is brought to settle the question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק "לא תבערו" is needed to teach that executions do not override שבת, because otherwise a קל וחומר would allow them.

steps.title: How to read "or perhaps not" under the earlier assumption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how "או אינו" would be explained according to its earlier assumption that the תנא relied on עשה דוחה לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to what the גמרא first assumed, that the reasoning was "a positive command comes and overrides a prohibition," what is the "or perhaps it is not" that the תנא said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its first understanding of the ברייתא and asks how the phrase "או אינו" would fit that reading. This opens the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא assumed that the ברייתא's first idea came from עשה דוחה לא תעשה, not from a קל וחומר. Under that reading, there is no קבורת מת מצוה refutation to explain the back-and-forth. So the גמרא needs a different explanation of "או אינו".

keyTerms.meaning: "What entered his mind at first": the original assumption
A positive command comes and overrides a prohibition

phrases.english: And according to what entered his mind at the outset,
phrases.notes: This points back to the גמרא's earlier assumption about how the ברייתא was reasoning.

phrases.english: that a positive command comes and overrides a prohibition,
what is the "or perhaps it is not" that he said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאי דִּסְלֵיק אַדַּעְתֵּיהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא דְּאָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained "או אינו" according to רב שמי בר אשי, the גמרא asks the same question according to the earlier reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How "או אינו" is explained if the ברייתא's first idea was based on עשה דוחה לא תעשה.

steps.title: Rereading או אינו as a positive מצוה overriding a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The תנא's thought was: the death penalty for breaking שבת covers other labors, but court execution overrides שבת, because an עשה overrides a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the תנא means: how do I apply the פסוק 'those who profane it shall surely be put to death'? It applies to all other kinds of work, but not to court executions. Court executions override שבת, because a positive מצוה comes and overrides a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. It explains what the תנא's 'או אינו' would mean if he were thinking of the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading the תנא's starting idea was not a קל וחומר. It was the general rule that an עשה pushes aside a לא תעשה. Carrying out a court's death sentence is an עשה, so he thought it should push aside the שבת prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I apply (this פסוק)?, a way of limiting a פסוק to some cases
Those who profane it (שבת) shall surely be put to death
An execution carried out by the court
A positive מצוה overrides a negative prohibition

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
How do I apply "those who profane it shall surely be put to death"?
To the other kinds of work
except for court executions.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין דָּחֵי שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: But a court execution overrides שבת,
because a positive מצוה comes and overrides a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 6 about how to read או אינו under the עשה דוחה לא תעשה approach.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא first thought that court execution overrides שבת because an עשה overrides a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Doubting whether a positive מצוה overrides a prohibition with כרת
steps.stepSummary: The תנא pulls back: the rule may only work for a plain לאו, not for one that carries כרת like שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he said: Fine, we say that a positive מצוה overrides a prohibition, but that is a plain prohibition. Did you ever hear that it overrides a prohibition that carries כרת?
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא questions his own idea from step 7. Maybe the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה does not reach a serious prohibition like שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 used a general rule. Now the תנא points out that שבת is not an ordinary לאו, because breaking it carries כרת. Maybe the rule only covers simple prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said, meaning he changed direction
Plain, by itself, with nothing extra
Spiritual cutting-off, a very severe punishment

phrases.english: Then he said:
Granted that we say
that a positive מצוה comes and overrides a prohibition,
that is a plain prohibition.
A prohibition that carries כרת,
did you ever hear that it overrides that?
phrases.notes: He means שבת, which is that kind of serious prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the reasoning of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה so it may not apply to שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 7 assumed the rule works even for a prohibition with כרת, and that has never been shown.

steps.title: How serious the prohibition is should not matter
steps.stepSummary: The תנא answers his own doubt: an עשה already overrides a לאו that is more serious than itself, so a bigger or smaller level of seriousness should make no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he said: When we say a positive מצוה overrides a prohibition, isn't the prohibition already more serious than the positive מצוה? Yet the positive מצוה still overrides it. So what difference does a small extra seriousness or a big one make?
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא rejects the doubt he raised in step 8. This brings back the idea that court execution should override שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even an ordinary לאו is already more serious than an עשה, yet the עשה wins. Since the תורה already lets the weaker מצוה beat a more serious one, adding כרת is just more of the same. So by logic the עשה should override שבת too.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? It opens a question that expects the answer 'of course'
More serious than it
A small stringency / a big stringency

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up here. The תנא is not saying a לאו is lighter than an עשה. He is saying the opposite: a לאו is already heavier, and the עשה still beats it.

phrases.english: Then he said:
When we say "a positive מצוה overrides a prohibition,"
isn't the prohibition more serious than it,
and yet the positive מצוה comes and overrides it?
So what difference is a small stringency
or a big stringency?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר: אַטּוּ עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the doubt raised in step 8 and goes back to the reasoning of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the line between a plain לאו and a לאו with כרת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 8 ignored that the rule already lets an עשה override something more serious than itself.

steps.title: The verse לא תבערו is needed
steps.stepSummary: Since logic would let court execution override שבת, the פסוק לא תבערו is needed to teach that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the פסוק says: "You shall not kindle a fire."
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא closes this reading. The פסוק is needed because logic alone would have let the עשה override שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, 'או אינו' was the תנא's back-and-forth about עשה דוחה לא תעשה שיש בו כרת. Because he ended up thinking the עשה would win, the פסוק has to step in.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק teaches
You shall not kindle (fire on שבת)

steps.whatToRemember: In this reading, the ברייתא's 'או אינו' is a back-and-forth about whether an עשה overrides a לאו with כרת. Since logic ends up saying yes, the פסוק לא תבערו is needed to say no for court executions on שבת.

phrases.english: Therefore the פסוק says: "You shall not kindle."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 9: logic alone would let the עשה win, so a פסוק is needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under this reading, לא תבערו is needed because logic would have let an עשה override even a לאו with כרת.

steps.title: A new reason the word עליה is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the עשה דוחה לא תעשה approach. It suggests instead that the word עליה is needed because of the rule about something that was part of a general rule and came out of it to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is needed for this reason: you might have thought that a brother's wife is 'something that was part of a general rule and came out of the rule to teach.' Such a thing comes out to teach not only about itself, but about the whole general rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new reason for why the word עליה is needed. This line only sets up the idea. The גמרא will finish explaining it right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said עליה was needed only because someone might think an עשה overrides a לאו with כרת. That never got a clear proof, so now it gives a different reason. A brother's wife was included in the עריות and came out of that rule through יבום. Someone might think her case teaches something about the whole group of עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed
It would have entered your mind to say, meaning you might have thought
A brother's wife

keyTerms.term: דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה בַּכְּלָל וְיָצָא מִן הַכְּלָל לְלַמֵּד
keyTerms.meaning: Something that was part of a general rule and came out of it to teach, one of the rules for learning from פסוקים

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole basis for the word עליה. It no longer depends on the open question of an עשה overriding a לאו with כרת.

phrases.english: Rather, it is needed,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. 'It' is the word עליה that the גמרא has been talking about.

phrases.english: because you might have thought to say:
Let this brother's wife be
something that was part of a general rule
and came out of the rule to teach,
phrases.notes: She is part of the forbidden relations, but יבום lets her come out of that rule.

phrases.english: which came out not to teach only about itself,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְלַמֵּד עַל הַכְּלָל כּוּלּוֹ יָצָא.
phrases.english: but to teach about the whole general rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עשה דוחה לא תעשה approach and offers a new reason the word עליה is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason why a word in the פסוק is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the brother's wife, who came out of the עריות rule for יבום, teaches about all the עריות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not finished yet; the גמרא will spell out the rest of this reason next.

steps.title: A ברייתא introduces the rule about something that left a general rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that states the rule of דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא מן הכלל and asks how it works.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Something that was part of a general rule and came out of the general rule to teach... How does this work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the idea from step 11. This line is a setup: it names the rule and asks for an example, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the word עליה is needed because of this rule. Now the גמרא shows where the rule comes from. The rule says that when the תורה singles out one item from a larger group, the item teaches something about the whole group, not just about itself.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches

keyTerms.term: דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה בַּכְּלָל וְיָצָא מִן הַכְּלָל
keyTerms.meaning: Something that was part of a general rule and was singled out; it teaches about the whole group
How so? (asking for an example)

phrases.english: As it is taught: Something that was in the general rule
and came out of the general rule, etc.,
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of the rule: it was singled out to teach about the whole group, not only about itself.

phrases.english: How so?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה בַּכְּלָל וְיָצָא מִן הַכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the rule mentioned in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An item singled out from a general group teaches about the whole group.

steps.title: The example of שלמים eaten while טמא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows the rule using the פסוק about eating שלמים while טמא, which teaches the law for all קדשי מזבח but not for קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the person who eats meat from the שלמים while his טומאה is on him". But weren't שלמים already part of all קדשים? Why were they singled out? To compare the others to them and tell you: just as שלמים are special in being holy for the מזבח, so too everything holy for the מזבח is included. That leaves out things given to בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its example. The תורה singled out שלמים for the punishment of eating while טמא, and that teaches the law for a whole group of קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every kind of קדשים is forbidden to eat while טמא, so naming שלמים alone seems unnecessary. The ברייתא says שלמים were named to define the group. The punishment applies to anything like שלמים, meaning holy for the מזבח. It does not apply to donations for the upkeep of the בית המקדש.

To compare one thing to another and apply the same law

steps.title: Applying the rule to a brother's wife
steps.stepSummary: Using the same rule, one might say: אשת אח was singled out from all עריות and allowed, so all עריות should be allowed too. This is why עליה is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: אשת אח was part of all the עריות, so why was she singled out? To compare the others to her and tell you: just as אשת אח is allowed, all עריות are also allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the ברייתא's rule to יבום. This fills out the suggestion from step 11 about why the word עליה is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother's wife is one of the forbidden relations, but the תורה took her out of that group and allowed her through יבום. By the rule, that could teach that every ערוה is allowed for יבום, and the word עליה would be needed to block this mistake. The next step questions whether this comparison works at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the pattern from the שלמים example and applies it to אשת אח.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source for why עליה is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without עליה one might apply the rule and allow all עריות through יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggested: the word עליה is needed to block that reading. Step 15 then challenges whether the comparison to שלמים holds.

steps.title: The comparison does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. With שלמים, the group and the detail are both forbidden. With אשת אח, the group is forbidden but the detail is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these really alike? There, the general rule is a prohibition and the detail is a prohibition. Here, the general rule is a prohibition and the detail is a permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 14. The rule from the ברייתא does not fit the case of אשת אח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With שלמים, the detail has the same kind of law as its group (both are forbidden), so it can teach about the group. A brother's wife is allowed, which is the opposite of her group, so she is not explaining the group. She is simply an exception. So this rule cannot be the reason עליה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they really alike?
General rule
The specific detail
Permission

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the rule of דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא is wrong. It only means the rule works when the detail shares the law of its group, and here it does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a limit on the rule: a detail that gets the opposite law cannot teach about its whole group.

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There: the general rule is a prohibition, and the detail is a prohibition.
Here: the general rule is a prohibition, and the detail is a permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם: כְּלָל בְּאִיסּוּר, וּפְרָט בְּאִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the application made in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא as the reason עליה is needed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the example, the detail shares the law of its group (both forbidden). Here the detail is allowed while its group is forbidden, so it does not teach about the group.

steps.title: A new comparison: something that left its group for a brand-new law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the case of אשת אח is really like a different rule. When something leaves its group to be given a new law, you cannot return it to that group unless the תורה says so explicitly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this case is only comparable to something that was part of a general group and left it to be given a new law. You cannot return it to its group until the תורה explicitly returns it.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the שלמים comparison, the גמרא offers a better fit: the rule of דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא לידון בדבר החדש. This sets up a new explanation for why עליה is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier rule, the detail left the group to teach something about the group's own law. Here, the detail leaves the group and gets a completely new law. Something like that is cut off from the group entirely and stays out unless a פסוק brings it back.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not comparable
Left its group to be given a new law
To return it to its general group
Explicitly

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the rule from Step 12 (יצא מן הכלל ללמד). There, the detail teaches about the whole group. Here, the detail gets a new law and is separated from the group.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא דָּמֵי אֶלָּא לְדָבָר שֶׁהָיָה בַּכְּלָל

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the case under a different rule of derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case of אשת אח was like שלמים, under יצא מן הכלל ללמד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case belongs under יצא לידון בדבר החדש, where the detail leaves its group and only returns if the תורה explicitly says so.

steps.title: A ברייתא states the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that states the same rule: something that left its group for a new law cannot be returned without an explicit פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Something that was part of a general group and left it to be given a new law may not be returned to its group until the תורה explicitly returns it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the rule it just used by quoting a ברייתא that says it word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the rule is an accepted teaching and not something invented for this case. The ברייתא will next show how the rule works with an example.

steps.title: The example: why does the פסוק compare אשם to חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives its example with the פסוק about the מצורע's offering. It asks why the תורה needed to say 'like the חטאת, so is the אשם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? 'And he shall slaughter the sheep in the place where the חטאת and the עולה are slaughtered, in the holy place, for like the חטאת, the אשם belongs to the כהן.' There is no need for the verse to say 'like the חטאת, the אשם.' So why does it say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts its example. It points to extra words in a פסוק and asks what they come to teach. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of an אשם are already taught elsewhere in the תורה. So comparing the מצורע's אשם to a חטאת looks unnecessary. The ברייתא assumes these words must be teaching something new.

steps.title: The מצורע's אשם got a new law, so one might think it skips the altar
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the מצורע's אשם was given a new law: its blood goes on the right thumb and big toe. So one might think it does not need blood and fats placed on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the מצורע's אשם left its group to be given a new law, the right thumb and the right big toe, one might think it does not need its blood and sacrificial parts placed on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins answering its question by stating what we might have mistakenly thought. The answer continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצורע's אשם is a perfect case of יצא לידון בדבר החדש. Its blood goes on the person, which no other אשם has. Under the rule, it would then lose the regular אשם laws, like placing blood and fats on the altar. The extra words in the פסוק will come to bring it back.
